newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up on selective buying.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended higher on Wednesday with more investors entering the B share markets to buy selected stocks on improved sentiment, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index surged 1.975 points, or 2.64 percent, to 76.870 on heavy volume of 27.245 million shares worth $15.07 million, compared with a turnover of $7.9 million on Tuesday.
Brokers said more follow-through buying emerged in the afternoon session after signs of growing volume during the morning, helping to push the index sharply up by the close.
"Investors, especially domestic players, built positions actively today, indicating strong confidence in their outlook for the market," one broker said.
"The index will likely test resistance at 78-80 points in the short term," another broker said. "If that level is broken, it will spark more follow-up buying."
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the star performer on talk of financial restructuring, up $0.104, or 8.25 percent, to $1.364 on volume of 831,400 shares. Dazhong declined to comment on the rumours.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the most actively traded stock on institutional buying, gaining $0.022, or 2.69 percent, to $0.838 on volume of 2.3 million shares.
Shenzhen's B share index rose 1.26 points, or 0.79 percent, to 160.78 on turnover of HK$89.4 million, compared with Tuesday's HK$90.4 million.
"Quite a few blue chip firms have reported decent 1996 results, and investors have a good idea of what the rest will look like," said an analyst at J&A Securities.
Buyers are focussing on large companies that have or are expected to post strong profits, analysts said.
"High-performing firms like Fangda are definitely the hot stocks at the moment," said a broker at China Guotai Securities.
Shenzhen Fangda Industry was the best performer, gaining HK$0.73, or 7.05 percent, to HK$11.09 on volume of 507,100 shares.
The Shanghai A share index ended up slightly in active trading, but technical charts showed signs of a possibile downward correction in the short term, brokers said.
The index edged up 2.177 points, or 0.16 percent, to 1,391.929 points on volume of 889.2 million shares worth 10.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index dipped 3.101 points, or 0.09 percent, to 3,593.295 points.
Shanghai 3F New Materials was the star A share, surging 1.05 yuan, or 10.03 percent, to 11.51 yuan on volume of 5.9 million shares due to speculative buying.
The Shenzhen A share index added 1.45 points, or 0.31 percent, to 461.27 on turnover of 9.02 billion yuan, compared with Tuesday's 7.74 billion.
